text:
karim: heads-up: container base image scan just flagged high severity issues in a bunch of our ubuntu/alpine images. OpenSSL and glibc fixes are recommended upstream. mapping by service below.

elaine: thanks — can you paste the exact CVEs + the image tags? quick triage so we can prioritize.

karim: sure. scan output (from vuln-scan):
- svc-auth: registry.redwood/svc-auth:prod-202402 -> CVE-2025-1428 (glibc, high), CVE-2025-2101 (openssl, high)
- svc-cache: registry.redwood/svc-cache:prod-202401 -> CVE-2025-2101 (openssl, high)
- analytics-worker: registry.redwood/analytics:latest -> alpine:3.16 base CVE-2025-1987 (libcrypto)

sre-bot: [auto] full report saved: https://infra/reports/scan/1745009876 (attachments: sbom.csv)

elaine: high-level plan proposal:
1) scope: list all images that inherit ubuntu:22.04 and alpine:3.16/3.17
2) repro & confirm: run `openssl version -a` and libc check inside current image
3) rebuild with pinned upstream patches (ubuntu:22.04.4 or alpine:3.19), push to canary repo tag
4) canary deploy 2 services in non-prod + 2 prod-light routes for 48h monitoring
5) full rollout with staged waves if canary ok
6) emergency rollback plan if we see >1% error spike

tim: I can enumerate images and start the CI branch for automated rebuilds. note: we have ~43 unique service images; ~12 multiarch. Rebuild time per image ~ 6-12m cold, ~2m cached. Need to disable cache for glibc/OpenSSL layer to ensure patched base gets used: `docker build --no-cache --pull -t registry.redwood/<svc>:patch-1745009876 .`

maria: add healthcheck / smoke tests to the pipeline before canary. Also we should run perf regression (p50/p95) since glibc changes can affect tail latency. plan window: start canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

karim: confirmed impact scope: public auth endpoints and a few internal RBAC services. No KMS keys affected, key rotations not required.

elaine: triage prioritization:
- P0 (within 24h): services exposed to external traffic with SSL termination (svc-auth, gateway, webhooks)
- P1 (48-72h): internal but customer-facing (analytics, notifications)
- P2 (7d): batch and dev-only images

ci-bot: kicked off branch: `infra/base-image/patch-1745009876` -> CI matrix: ubuntu22.04 / alpine3.19 / amd64 / arm64. See: https://ci.redwood/pipelines/6443

tim: will push images to `registry.redwood/canary/<svc>:patch-1745009876` and update k8s canary manifest to use that tag for 1 replica in each cluster (canary namespace).

elaine: add these checks before promoting image:
- `openssl version -a` shows >= patched version for CVE-2025-2101
- `ldd --version` or `strings /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6 | head -n1` confirms glibc patch
- run unit + smoke + perf suite (20m)
- quick sec scan of rebuilt image (trivy) must pass with no high/critical left except allowed list

karim: any constraints from compliance/regulatory teams? we have one customer on dedicated private who requires image rebuilds to be audited. I propose we record the image digest and store in the compliance bucket and add a signed SBOM.

elaine: yes, for Dedicated customers we need: artifact digest, SBOM, signed attestations. Tim can we automate SBOM generation in the rebuild pipeline?

tim: yep — pipeline step `make sbom` already exists. will add `cosign` signing step and push SBOM to `s3://compliance-sboms/1745009876/`

maria: rollback plan: if any canary fails, we revert k8s deployment to previous digest using the tag `prod-previous`, and run an incident runbook. No DB migrations in these images so rollback is quick.

elaine: timeline/owners:
- today (<12h): inventory and confirm list of affected images (tim, karim)
- 24h: start canary rebuilds + push canary tags (tim)
- 48h: finish canary monitoring and signoff (elaine + svc owners)
- 7d: full rollout (maria + platform)

karim: one small gotcha — some Dockerfiles do pinned apt packages in the Dockerfile that shadow distro glibc updates. we need to ensure base pkg cache is updated: add `apt-get update && apt-get dist-upgrade -y` in Dockerfile before other package installs. sample snippet:
```Dockerfile
FROM ubuntu:22.04
RUN apt-get update && apt-get dist-upgrade -y && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
# rest of Dockerfile
```

tim: also watch image size; dist-upgrade may change layers. consider using `--no-install-recommends` and cleanup.

elaine: final ask: svc owners, please ack in thread which of your services are P0/P1/P2 and point to any special test requirements. We'll triage exceptions (e.g., images that cannot be rebuilt due to ancient base layers) separately.

karim: ack from svc-auth, svc-gateway -> P0. I'll create tickets for dedicated customer artifact export.

maria: ack on adding perf regression to canary checks. I'll prep dashboards to watch p50/p95 & error rate.

sre-bot: [auto-update] ticket created: SEC-2025-321 (base-image rebuilds)

elaine: great. I'll send a follow-up w/ the exact canary manifests and checklist. if anyone needs to block this due to scheduled deploys, speak now, otherwise we proceed. :thumbsup:
